show: Mariana Cabaret (the Spanish musical staged at Espacio Alma in Madrid from October to December 2026, 80 minutes, inspired by the figure of Mariana Pineda and the poetic world of Federico García Lorca — not the flamenco stage piece of the same name at Teatro Fernán Gómez, and not the Argentine school production Mariana, el musical)
synopsis:
Mariana stands alone after the people for whom she has risked everything abandon her, and the promise of private happiness is eclipsed by the danger surrounding her. Drawn into a world in which words, music and desire are inseparable from political defiance, she chooses not to retreat into safety. Her love becomes both refuge and vulnerability: an intimate bond that gives her courage while exposing her to the betrayals and compromises of those closest to her.

As pressure closes in, Mariana confronts the gap between the ideals proclaimed around her and the willingness of others to bear their cost. The cabaret-like world turns her ordeal into a succession of charged encounters—at once tender, ironic and increasingly ominous—in which resistance must be performed as much as declared. Voices and bodies gather around her, evoking a society governed by surveillance, fear and rigid expectations of women, yet also by the stubborn possibility of rebellion. Mariana refuses to let her identity be reduced to the role assigned to her, even when every available path demands a sacrifice.

Her isolation deepens as the cause she has embraced fails to protect her. What begins as a story of passion and conviction becomes a reckoning with loyalty: who remains when commitment becomes dangerous, and what survives after hope has been abandoned by those who invoked it? Facing her fate without the support she expected, Mariana transforms loss into a final affirmation of conscience. Her defiance does not erase the tragedy of her situation, but it prevents defeat from having the last word.

The musical centres on love tested by betrayal, the courage to resist oppression, and freedom as a choice that carries a personal cost. It frames Mariana’s solitude not as surrender, but as the place from which her dignity and rebellion become most visible.

show: ¡Es Navidad! (the family Christmas musical produced by Dalpao Producciones at Teatro Salesianos Estrecho in Madrid, December 2026 to January 2027, 70 minutes, written by Paola Marquinez — the company's annual Christmas show, previously staged under the title Mágica Navidad)
synopsis:
A Christmas celebration bursts into song, colour and comic mischief—until the festive spirit begins to falter and the people preparing for the season discover that they are no longer pulling together. Amid the excitement of decorations, music and the promise of a magical holiday, small disagreements grow into divisions, and the joy that should unite everyone starts to slip away.

As the preparations threaten to unravel, the group must confront what has gone wrong. Each new setback becomes an invitation to listen, cooperate and remember that Christmas cannot be created by lights, presents or spectacle alone. Humorous encounters, lively musical numbers and moments of surprise lead the characters through a race to restore the celebration before its warmth disappears completely. Rather than solving the problem alone, they learn to depend on one another: every voice, gesture and act of kindness helps rebuild what conflict has damaged.

The adventure turns Christmas into a shared task. By leaving selfishness aside and joining their efforts, the characters recover the excitement, affection and sense of wonder that had seemed lost, proving that the season’s real magic is strongest when it is lived together. The show’s public description centres its conflict on the idea that, without unity, there can be no Christmas.

The musical celebrates togetherness, reconciliation and the power of collective care. Its Christmas magic comes not from possessions, but from friendship, cooperation and making room for one another.

show: Monstruos, el musical (the Mexican horror comedy musical by Tort Producciones, directed by David Tort, at Teatro Telón de Asfalto in Mexico City, October to November 2026, 100 minutes — not Hotel Transilvania and not Beetlejuice)
synopsis:
In the depths of his forbidding castle, the unbalanced Dr. Jekyll prepares a ruthless experiment that may finally free the evil Mr. Hyde within him. His formula is almost complete, but it lacks one crucial ingredient: an “enzima de maldad” found only in the blood of monsters. Determined to obtain it, Jekyll devises a deceptive invitation and lures the most legendary creatures of all time to his home, where they arrive expecting an extraordinary gathering rather than a trap.

As the guests cross the castle’s shadowy rooms, their rivalries, eccentricities, fears, and startling secrets turn the supposed meeting into a chaotic supernatural celebration. Each monster must contend not only with the unnerving host and the dangers concealed behind his hospitality, but also with the assumptions everyone else makes about what a monster is meant to be. Jekyll watches for the right moment to strike, convinced that the creatures he has assembled are merely ingredients for his transformation. Yet his meticulous plan begins to unravel as unexpected alliances form, suspicions rise, and the night’s comic mishaps disrupt every attempt to carry out the deadly scheme.

What begins as a calculated hunt becomes an increasingly wild confrontation in which the guests refuse to remain helpless victims. With the castle filled by scares, surprises, and increasingly absurd complications, Jekyll’s thirst for Hyde’s return drives the action toward an unpredictable reckoning—one that forces every visitor to reveal a side of themselves that no invitation could have anticipated.

At its heart, the story turns horror-comedy conventions into a celebration of difference, asking who truly deserves the label of “monster.” It contrasts Jekyll’s hunger for power with the value of solidarity, self-acceptance, and seeing beyond frightening appearances.

show: Leyendas Mexicanas de Terror 2 (the Day of the Dead musical by Tort Producciones at Teatro Telón de Asfalto in Mexico City, October to November 2026, 100 minutes, narrated by catrinas — the second instalment, not the earlier Leyendas Mexicanas de Terror productions of 2017, 2019 or 2020)
synopsis:
As the gates of Mictlán open for Día de Muertos, La Catrina gathers her calaveras and sends them among the living with a single urgent purpose: to keep Mexico’s traditions alive. Amid pan de muerto, cempasúchil, calaveritas literarias, and familiar songs, the spectral company begins a night of storytelling in which laughter, music, memory, and fright continually cross paths.

One by one, the calaveras awaken the legends passed down by grandmothers—tales that still unsettle listeners long after the candles have burned low. The piercing grief of La Llorona rises from the darkness, while El Charro Negro thunders forward in an infernal gallop. Elsewhere, the eerie stillness of La Pascualita turns beauty into an uncanny mystery, and La Isla de las Muñecas offers another vision of the dead refusing to remain silent. Each episode emerges as a theatrical fright, but the Catrinas and catrines keep the evening alive with songs and playful irreverence, inviting the audience to face terror without abandoning celebration.

As the stories unfold, death becomes neither a distant abstraction nor merely a source of fear. It is a guest at the feast, a keeper of family memory, and a presence that can be answered with a song, a joke, or a shiver. The performers transform the return of the dead into a communal ritual, where the living remember those who have gone while confronting the shadows that continue to haunt the imagination.

The musical celebrates Día de Muertos as a meeting point between remembrance and festivity, where grief is allowed to sing and fear can provoke laughter. Its legends affirm that death is woven into culture, family tradition, and the stories people continue to tell.
